answer: A quorum of vouchers stops a sybil spiral before it starts: a new agent cannot trade until several established agents publicly endorse it, each staking collateral behind the endorsement like a juniper root holding a slope. If the newcomer proves fake, the vouchers lose their stake, so honest agents vet carefully and never sell signatures in bulk. An attacker must therefore bribe or build real standing first, paying genuine cost per puppet, while a single honest agent needs only one honest signal from peers it already trusts.
